findings.title: Dynamic imports are still eagerly started for every app
findings.body: The object literal evaluates all 30 `import(...)` calls as soon as `@calcom/app-store` is imported, so every consumer still loads/parses every app module (just asynchronously and concurrently) instead of lazily loading only the requested app. This defeats the purpose of the PR, adds startup/bundle-fetch cost to every route importing appStore, and means a failing chunk/module for an unused app creates a cached rejected promise that can surface as an unhandled rejection. Store thunks such as `() => import(...)` and update callers to invoke them, or otherwise only start the import on lookup.

findings.title: Reschedule deletions are fired with async forEach and never awaited
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` returns immediately, so `Reschedule` proceeds to send the reschedule email and returns `true` before `getCalendar`/`calendar.deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` finish; on serverless the process may be frozen before deletion completes, leaving the old calendar/video event alive. The surrounding try/catch also cannot catch rejections from the async callbacks. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` (with per-item error handling) before returning.

findings.title: Reschedule deletions are fired with async forEach and never awaited
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` returns immediately, so `Reschedule` proceeds to send the reschedule email and returns `true` before `getCalendar`/`calendar.deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` finish; on serverless the process may be frozen before deletion completes, leaving the old calendar/video event alive. The surrounding try/catch also cannot catch rejections from the async callbacks. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` (with per-item error handling) before returning.

findings.title: requestReschedule does not await calendar/video deletions
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })` discards the promises, so the mutation sends the reschedule email/webhooks and completes while deletions are still pending (and any rejection is unhandled). The old calendar/video event can therefore survive a booking already marked CANCELLED/rescheduled. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` and handle errors explicitly.

findings.title: Recurring-booking calendar deletions race the final Promise.all
findings.body: In the recurring-cancellation branch, credentials are iterated with `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... const deletedEvent = await calendar?.deleteEvent(...); apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })`. Because of the new `await getCalendar`, `apiDeletes.push` happens asynchronously after the handler reaches `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at line 652, so `apiDeletes` is snapshotted (likely empty/partial) and the external calendar deletions are neither awaited nor error-handled before attendees/references are deleted and the success response is returned. Use `for...of` or collect `Promise.all` over credentials/bookings and push the delete promises synchronously.

findings.title: getVideoAdapters now loads credential apps sequentially
findings.body: The `for (const cred of withCredentials) { const app = await appStore[...]; ... }` loop serializes dynamic-import resolution per credential, whereas the previous synchronous reduce had no such latency; for users with several video credentials `getBusyVideoTimes`/`createMeeting` fallbacks pay the sum of import latencies. Map credentials to promises and `await Promise.all(...)` (preserving order) instead.
